sheet-15-1.description: The main part of sheet 15 of the 1928 Mount Holly atlas covers Clermont, the district on the western edge of Mount Holly where the town meets Hainesport and Lumberton Townships, at 100 feet to an inch. Washington runs across the sheet from Maple Avenue at the left edge past Cumberland, Middlesex and Hunderton to Carlton Avenue, with 1st Street parallel to it at the top. North of Washington are the large blocks 157 to 161 and the Northampton Textile Co., a weaving mill reached by a road running north. South of Washington the residential blocks 165 and 166 lie between Cumberland, Middlesex and Hunderton, and blocks 167 and 208 between Washington, Carlton Court, Holeman and Carlton Avenue, mostly frame dwellings, with the 2nd Baptist Church (colored) at Washington and Carlton Avenue. Below them the P.R.R. Toms River Branch crosses the sheet in a broad curve with sidings; beside it stands the Royle & Pilkington Co., manufacturers of tapestry goods, with several mill buildings and a machine shop, and further east the Rem Co. with a cement block manufacturing shed and storage. The lower right shows a newer subdivision, block 241, between Ridge Avenue, Carlton Avenue (marked not opened), Cedar (not opened) and Caley Avenue, with a few dwellings at its west end near Ridge Avenue. Dash-dot lines mark the Hainesport, Northampton and Lumberton Township boundaries. The blank area west of Cumberland and south of Washington is marked 15: it is drawn in the inset in the lower left of this sheet. The compass rose, scale bar and the Sanborn copyright line of 1928 are in the lower right.
notes: Hunderton is today Hunterdon Avenue (North Hunterdon Avenue north of Washington Street); the sheet spells it Hunderton.
Cumberland is today North Cumberland Avenue and South Cumberland Avenue; Middlesex is Middlesex Avenue; Holeman is Holeman Street.
The road north from Washington Street east of block 161 matches Lippincott Lane.
Carlton Court is not in OpenStreetMap under that name; Gillman Street and South Somerset Avenue were tried as its modern line and disagreed with the fit by 8 to 12 m, so they were left out.
Carlton Avenue south of the railroad and Cedar are marked not opened.

Printed sheet 15 of the Mount Holly, N.J. atlas (Nov. 1928), covering Clermont on the west edge of Mount Holly (Burlington County), not Clermont in Cape May County; the catalog box is right. Scale 100 ft to an inch, north about 36 degrees clockwise from up. Part 1 (main map): Washington Street from Maple Av to Carlton Av, Cumberland, Middlesex, Hunderton (Hunterdon Avenue), 1st St, Holeman, Carlton Ct and Carlton Av, the P.R.R. Toms River Branch with Royle & Pilkington Co., and Ridge, Carlton (not opened), Caley Avs and Cedar in the lower right. Part 2 (inset at lower left, behind a heavy line, same scale and rotation): Washington St west of Cumberland with Maple Av and Brotherhood Cemetery; it fills the blank area marked 15 west of Cumberland in part 1.

sheet-15-2.description: The inset in the lower left of sheet 15 of the 1928 Mount Holly atlas, set off by a heavy line, shows the part of Clermont west of Cumberland that the main map leaves blank, at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch and the same orientation, with its own north arrow. Washington, 60 feet wide with an 8 inch water pipe, crosses it from the left edge to Cumberland at the right border. North of Washington is block 158, lettered Clermont, with a few frame dwellings at nos. 605 to 613 and a hen house. South of Washington lie the large block 163, occupied by the Brotherhood Cemetery, and block 164 between Maple Avenue and Cumberland, which holds a Lutheran parsonage, dwellings and a garage with auto repair at its south end, with a dashed outline on the west side of Maple Avenue. Most of the inset is open ground; the only streets are Washington, Maple Avenue and Cumberland, whose east side is cut off by the inset border. The figures 15 to the right of Cumberland refer to the main part of this sheet.
notes: Placed from one junction (Maple Avenue / Washington Street) with the scale and rotation of the main part; the Cumberland / Washington junction, measured at the inset border, agreed within about 2 m but was left out because two points 80 m apart fixed the rotation poorly.
Washington is Washington Street today; Cumberland is South Cumberland Avenue.
